frameworks.name: Decision-Making Speed Framework
frameworks.definition: Accelerating decision velocity by reducing deliberation time from weekly to hourly to real-time, enabled by understanding decision reversibility and the speed loss from delayed choice.

frameworks.name: Decision-Reversal Calculus
frameworks.definition: Evaluating decisions by the cost delta between forward action and reversal, comparing total time cost (decision delay plus reversal cost) to find the optimal choice moment.

claims.text: Most decisions in life are reversible or have low-cost correction paths; the real economic cost of a decision is the delta between acquisition price and resale price, not the choice itself.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: does not apply to irreversible life choices (relocations with family/career consequences)
bounded_by: Does not apply to irreversible family or legal decisions
Does not apply to decisions with long time-recovery windows

claims.text: Decision deliberation time compounds faster than doing time; if a 5-minute decision followed by a 10-minute fix takes 15 minutes total, but deliberation takes 2 hours, the deliberation approach is slower by ~8x.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

numbers.axis: total time cost (decision + reversal vs. deliberation)

anchors.value: 5 minutes decision + 10 minutes fix = 15 minutes total

bounded_by: Does not apply when fix costs exceed initial decision costs
Does not apply to irreversible decisions

claims.text: Unmade decisions are the heaviest cognitive burden in life, consuming attention and brain power more than any external constraint; deciding immediately liberates attention.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: pending decisions consume working memory and create psychological drag that prevents parallel action

claims.text: Pursuing certainty before acting is a false frame; the only certain dreams are old dreams that have already occurred, making them unfalsifiable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not apply to routine operational decisions where certainty is achievable

claims.text: Operators can move through life at 7x the pace by shifting decision cadence from weekly to daily; further acceleration moves to hourly or real-time decision points.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Does not apply to high-consequence decisions (capital allocation >$1M, personnel terminations)

claims.text: Test-and-learn iteration cycles are faster and more informative than up-front deliberation; the data from a wrong fast decision teaches more than delayed theorizing.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies when decision cost is low and reversal cost is bounded
claims.mechanism: fast iteration compresses the feedback loop, surfacing variables that theoretical deliberation misses

claims.text: The primary constraint on growth is not the doing, but the deciding; teams and founders slow down at decision points more than at execution.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Real mistakes are preferable to the bigger mistake of decision paralysis; even monster-sized execution mistakes accumulate less cost than indefinite non-decision.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: does not apply to capital losses or legal liability
bounded_by: Does not apply to irreversible decisions (permanent IP loss, regulatory penalties)

claims.text: Decision cost includes the opportunity cost of the time spent waiting; a six-month deliberation delay on a job-site vehicle costs the revenue and client relationships forgone during that delay period.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies when the input generates revenue
claims.mechanism: delayed acquisition of productive assets slows revenue generation, creating compounding opportunity loss

claims.text: Discomfort is inherent to meaningful goals; the willingness to endure unmade decisions, uncertainty, and risk directly correlates with access to better futures.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: A business owner delays purchasing a truck for six months while deliberating whether it's the right choice. During those six months, they cannot attend job sites, pick up clients, or scale operations. The real cost of the decision is not the truck's price, but the revenue lost during the delay period. If the truck costs $40k to buy and $35k to sell (delta $5k), but six months of delayed operation costs $30k in lost revenue, the true decision cost is the lost revenue, not the truck price delta.

When deciding which vendor to hire, which website design to use, or which ad hook to test, a team leader calls a real-time decision rather than deferring to a future meeting. The team picks immediately—"Which vendor? Pick. Website? Pick. Headline? Pick." This compressed cadence allows the business to move forward on all fronts, while a team that defers these decisions to "next week" loses the compounding effect of 7 days of execution delay repeated across 10-15 decisions.

practices.text: Confront decision points directly and immediately rather than deferring to future meetings; if the data needed to decide is incomplete, decide anyway and iterate.
Surface the handful of deferred decisions you know you need to make and decide them today; unmade decisions consume more attention than any external problem.
Evaluate decision cost as the sum of (deliberation time + reversal cost + opportunity cost during delay), not the nominal choice itself.
When uncertain, move from weekly decision cadence to daily, then hourly, then real-time, testing the impact on forward speed.
